Hence log2 W_OBDD <= W_rank <= W_OBDD.

proved_step: PROOF. Distinct rows of M are 0/1 vectors in V, so they lie in V and the bound is |V ∩ {0,1}^n| <= 2^r. Let B be an r x n matrix whose rows are a basis of V. B has rank r, so it has r linearly independent columns; let S be their index set, |S| = r. For v = cB in V (c in Q^r), v_S = c B_S, and B_S is invertible, so c is determined by v_S and hence v is determined by v_S. So the restriction x -> x_S is injective on V. It maps V ∩ {0,1}^n into {0,1}^S, which has 2^r elements. Hence |V ∩ {0,1}^n| <= 2^r. For the corollary: fix an order pi that attains W_rank. Every cut k has distinct-row count <= 2^{rank_k} <= 2^{W_rank}, so the max over cuts is <= 2^{W_rank}; minimising over orders gives W_OBDD <= 2^{W_rank}. Check: F={x0+x1+x2=1} has W_rank=2, W_OBDD=3 <= 4. The lemma is elementary and is probably standard in the rank-versus-OBDD literature; it is recorded as a verified finite-scope step, not as new. proved_step: Proof. Let s_j(i) be the partial sum of gate j over the first i variables. Let P_j(i) = sum_{l>i} max(W_jl,0) and N_j(i) = sum_{l>i} min(W_jl,0), so the final sum lies in [s_j+N_j, s_j+P_j]. Define the class kappa_j(s) = 0 if s+P_j(i) < t_j; 1 if s+N_j(i) >= t_j; and the exact value s otherwise. (1) Exactness: for class 0 or 1 the bottom bit is the same for every completion of the remaining variables; for an undecided s the class is the exact value. So the bit vector of any completion depends only on the class vector. (2) Transitions are well defined: reading x_{i+1} changes P and N by subtracting max(W,0) and min(W,0) at index i+1. If class 0, then s'+P(i+1) <= s+P(i) < t, so s' stays class 0. Class 1 is symmetric. Undecided values are updated exactly. So the class vector at stage i+1 is a function of the class vector at stage i and x_{i+1}. (3) Counting: the DP c_{i+1}(kappa') = sum over (kappa, x_{i+1}) with transition kappa -> kappa' of c_i(kappa) is exact, and at i = n the classes are bits, so #f^{-1}(1) = sum of c_n over class vectors with top(bits) = 1. (4) State bound: at stage i an undecided value of gate j lies in an interval of length P_j(i) - N_j(i) = sum_{l>i}|W_jl| <= B(n-i), so there are at most B(n-i)+2 classes per gate and at most prod_j (B(n-i)+2) class vectors. Summing over i gives O(k n (Bn+2)^k) operations. Scope: fixed k, bounded integer weights; all other bottom gates are irrelevant to f and drop out. Compared with the plain partial-sum DP (state bound (2Bi+1)^k at stage i), the gain is a constant-factor change in the window, not a change of the exponent. Barrier and transfer check: this is a poly(n) algorithm for constant k and B = poly(n), so it cannot transfer to a 2^n/n^{omega(1)} lower-bound hypothesis; no LOWER_BOUND is claimed. Known-type status: counting for a constant number of halfspaces over a bounded-weight cube is standard (Dyer / Frieze-style pseudo-polynomial DP); I have not checked the literature, so novelty is unverified.

proved_step: LEMMA (rank sandwich for OBDD width). Let f:{0,1}^n->{0,1}, let pi be a variable order, and for 1<=l<=n-1 let M_l(f,pi) be the 0/1 matrix with rows indexed by assignments a to the first l variables, columns by assignments b to the remaining variables, entries f(a,b). Let R_l = rank over GF(2) of M_l, and D_l = number of DISTINCT rows of M_l (= number of distinct subfunctions f|_a). Then R_l <= D_l <= 2^{R_l}. Consequently minRank(f) <= min_pi max_l D_l(f,pi) <= 2^{minRank(f)}, where minRank(f) = min_pi max_l R_l(f,pi). PROOF. Let V be the GF(2) row space of M_l, dim V = R_l, so |V| = 2^{R_l}. Every row lies in V, and the rows span V by definition, so the set of distinct rows is a spanning set of V; hence D_l >= R_l. Also the distinct rows are elements of V, so D_l <= |V| = 2^{R_l}. For the consequence: for each pi, max_l R_l <= max_l D_l, so minRank <= min_pi max_l D_l. For pi* attaining minRank, max_l D_l(f,pi*) <= 2^{max_l R_l(f,pi*)} = 2^{minRank}, so min_pi max_l D_l <= 2^{minRank}. Each step is elementary linear algebra over GF(2); no computation is used. SCOPE: all Boolean f, all n>=2, all orders. STATUS OF THE GAP: this sandwich is two-sided but does not decide G0001. The lower side is trivial (D >= R). The upper side gives only the exponential relation, not the reverse direction that G0001 asks for. It is not a P vs NP claim and carries no barrier content (no lower bound is proved).

lemma: S-54f648a904 (formal). Let F = C_1 AND ... AND C_m be a CNF on variables 0..n-1, each clause a set of literals. For S subset of {1..m} let V(S) be the set of variables occurring in clauses of S, and say S is consistent if the assignments that falsify every literal of every clause in S exist, i.e. no variable is required both 0 and 1. Then #F = sum_{S} (-1)^|S| N(S), with N(S) = 2^(n - |V(S)|) if S is consistent and N(S) = 0 otherwise.
proved_step: Proof: an assignment x falsifies C_i for all i in S iff, for each literal l in C_i, x makes l false; so the set of such x is {x : x agrees with the forced values of S}. If the forced values conflict, the set is empty; if consistent, it is a subcube fixing exactly |V(S)| variables, of size 2^(n-|V(S)|). Inclusion-exclusion over the falsified-clause events A_i = {x falsifies C_i} gives #(no A_i) = sum_S (-1)^|S| |intersection_{i in S} A_i|, which is the formula. Clauses with complementary literals are never falsified and are handled by the conflict case. Status: CLAIMED, the argument is elementary and standard; the value is a precise statement, not new mathematics. The sum has 2^m terms, so it gives no polynomial-time algorithm.

proved_step: L-HWB-RANK (CLAIMED, derived in session R1498; needs review by another model family). Setup: HWB_n(x)=x_{|x|} for |x|>=1, 0 for |x|=0. Fix p in {0..n}, a=(x_1..x_p), b=(x_{p+1}..x_n), M_p[a,b]=HWB_n(a,b). Claim: rank_Q(M_p) <= (p+1)^2 <= (n+1)^2. Proof: HWB(x)=sum_{t=1}^n [|x|=t] x_t. Put s=|a|. For t<=p the term is a_t [|b|=t-s]; for t>p it is [|b|=t-s] b_{t-p}. So row a equals F_s(b) + sum_{t=1}^p a_t H_{t-s}(b), with s=|a|, H_u(b)=[|b|=u], F_s(b)=sum_{t=p+1}^n [|b|=t-s] b_{t-p}. Each row lies in V_s = span{F_s, H_{t-s}: 1<=t<=p}, dim <= p+1, and V_s depends only on s in {0..p}. So the row space lies in sum_{s=0}^p V_s, of dimension <= (p+1)^2. Consequence (conditional on H below): the natural order gives W_rank(HWB_n) <= (n+1)^2, so min over orders is <= (n+1)^2. H (CITED, NOT VERIFIED AT SOURCE; secondary arXiv 1912.01430 Prop. 4 proof attributes it to Bryant [10] with an improvement in Wegener's book Thm 4.10.2): every OBDD for HWB_n, for every variable order, has size >= 2^{n/5}. Then max level width >= (2^{n/5}-2)/(n+1), so W_OBDD(HWB_n) >= 2^{Omega(sqrt(W_rank))}, which refutes any polynomial bound W_OBDD <= poly(W_rank) on the HWB family, conditional on H. Scope: the rank bound is unconditional for all n and all p; the separation is conditional on H.

proved_step: Proof. Rows of M lie in V = rowspace_F(M), dim V = r. Distinct rows span V, so D >= r. Let B be an r x N matrix whose rows form a basis of V, and S a set of r columns with B_S invertible over F. For v = cB in V, v_S = c B_S, so v is determined by v_S; restriction to S is injective on V. Distinct 0/1 rows of M are distinct elements of V whose restrictions lie in {0,1}^S, a set of 2^r elements, so D <= 2^r. The order consequence follows by applying this to each cut, since distinct subfunctions at a cut equal distinct rows of its cut matrix.

proved_step: S-AND-WIDTH-01: Let F, G: {0,1}^k -> {0,1} be Boolean functions on the same prefix-cut, with residual functions f_a = F(a, .) and g_a = G(a, .) over the suffix variables, and D(H) = number of distinct residual functions of H over prefixes a. Then D(F AND G) <= D(F) D(G). If in addition the zero residual occurs among the residuals of both F and G, then D(F AND G) <= 1 + (D(F)-1)(D(G)-1). Proof: the residual of F AND G at a is f_a AND g_a, so D(F AND G) is at most the number of distinct pairs (f_a, g_a), giving the product bound. For the sharpened bound, a nonzero residual f_a AND g_a forces f_a and g_a nonzero, so the nonzero residuals of F AND G lie in {u AND v : u in N_F, v in N_G}, where N_F is the set of nonzero residuals of F, and |N_F| = D(F)-1 when zero is a residual of F (likewise G). This gives at most (D(F)-1)(D(G)-1) nonzero residuals plus one zero residual. Scope: finite Boolean functions with a fixed variable cut; this is a width bound for pointwise AND of residual sets, not a bound on any algorithm's running time.

proved_step: S-sandwich-rank-OBDD (LEMMA, CLAIMED). Scope: any Boolean f on {0,1}^n, any variable order, any cut k. Let M_k be the 2^k x 2^(n-k) matrix M_k[a,b] = f(a,b) with prefix a and suffix b. Let D_k = number of distinct rows of M_k and R_k = rank over Q of M_k. Claim: R_k <= D_k <= 2^(R_k). Proof. (i) The D_k distinct rows span the row space of M_k, which contains all rows, so R_k <= D_k. (ii) Let V be the row space of M_k, dim V = R_k. Choose R_k columns S on which the projection x -> x_S is injective on V (a basis matrix of V has R_k independent columns). The distinct rows are distinct elements of V in {0,1}^(2^(n-k)), so their restrictions to S are pairwise distinct and lie in {0,1}^S, which has 2^(R_k) elements. Hence D_k <= 2^(R_k). Consequence: write W_rank(pi) = max_k R_k and W_OBDD(pi) = max_k D_k. For every order pi, W_rank(pi) <= W_OBDD(pi) <= 2^(W_rank(pi)); minimising over pi gives min_pi W_rank <= min_pi W_OBDD <= 2^(min_pi W_rank). Gap relation: G0001 asks whether min_pi W_OBDD <= poly(min_pi W_rank). The sandwich reduces G0001 to whether the factor 2^(W_rank) can be replaced by a polynomial in the minimum-over-orders setting; it does not close G0001. Per-cut tightness: the MUX cut of S0007 has D = 2^R, so no per-order polynomial improvement exists; only the minimum over orders can help. statement: For every n >= 2, every order of the n variables and every cut with prefix set A (|A| = k): rank_Q(M_A) <= (k+1)(n-k+1) <= floor((n+2)^2/4), where M_A is the cut matrix of HWB_n(x) = x_{|x|} (0 if |x| = 0) with rows indexed by prefix assignments a and columns by suffix assignments b.
proof: Split rows of M_A by the weight s in {0..k} of a and columns by the weight t in {0..n-k} of b. This gives (k+1)(n-k+1) blocks R_{s,t}, and M_A is the sum of their zero-padded versions. On R_{s,t}, |a union b| = s+t = j is constant, so the entry equals x_j for a fixed variable j. If j = 0 the block is zero. If j in A, the entry is a_j, which depends only on the row, so the block has rank <= 1. If j in B, the entry is b_j, which depends only on the column, so the block has rank <= 1. Rank is subadditive, so rank_Q(M_A) <= (k+1)(n-k+1). Maximising over k gives floor((n+2)^2/4).

statement: Let M be a matrix over Q with k columns and r = rank_Q(M). The number of distinct 0/1 rows of M is at most 2^r. Consequently, for a fixed variable order, the number of distinct residual functions at a cut is at most 2^{rank_Q(M_cut)}. Scope: fixed order only; min over orders is NOT covered (G0001 stays open).
proof: Let V = rowspace(M), dim V = r. Choose r columns J with a nonzero r x r minor. The projection pi_J: V -> Q^J has image of dimension rank(M restricted to J) = r, so it is injective on V. Each distinct 0/1 row lies in V and maps injectively into {0,1}^J, which has 2^r elements. The GF(2) inequality rank_GF2(M) <= rank_Q(M) holds because a minor nonzero mod 2 is nonzero over Q.

proved_step: BUCKET-ELIM-EXACT (standard, Dechter 1999; recorded as bookkeeping, closes no obligation). Let F(x_1..x_n) = prod_{i=1..k} f_i(x_{S_i}) with f_i : {0,1}^{S_i} -> Z_{>=0}. Fix an order v_1..v_n. At step t, let I_t be the factors whose scope contains v_t, U_t the union of their scopes, and g_t(x_{U_t \ {v_t}}) = sum_{x_{v_t} in {0,1}} prod_{i in I_t} f_i. Then (a) the sum of F over {0,1}^n equals the value of the final scalar product obtained by the recursion (distributivity of product over sum, since v_t occurs only in the factors of I_t at step t); (b) the product table at step t has 2^{|U_t|} entries and g_t has 2^{|U_t|-1} entries; (c) so the largest table is at most 2^{w+1}, w = max_t (|U_t| - 1). Proof: (a) induction on t, using that v_t occurs in no factor outside I_t at that point; (b) by definition of U_t. Scope: finite Boolean, nonnegative weights, any fixed order. Consequence: exact counting for positive 1-in-3 CNF costs sum_t 2^{|U_t|} arithmetic operations, with the 3-variable clause table having 3 of 8 entries nonzero.

statement: Let M be a 0/1 matrix over Q with rank_Q(M) = r. Then M has at most 2^r distinct rows. Consequently, for a fixed variable order and cut k, the number of distinct residual functions D_k <= 2^{r_k}, where r_k = rank_Q of the cut communication matrix, and the OBDD width of that order is <= 2^{max_k r_k}.
derivation: Let V in Q^B be the row space of M, dim V = r. Choose a basis of V, form the r x |B| matrix of basis vectors, and pick r columns J on which it is invertible. The projection pi_J: V -> Q^J is then injective. Every row of M lies in V and has entries in {0,1}, so pi_J(row) lies in {0,1}^J, which has 2^r elements. Hence a row is determined by at most 2^r values and M has at most 2^r distinct rows. Applying this to the cut matrix of each level k gives D_k <= 2^{r_k}. Scope: this is an exponential bound 2^{O(W_rank)} only; it does not give the polynomial form poly(W_rank) asked in the gap.

statement: For every r >= 1 there is a 0/1 matrix M_r with rank_Q(M_r) = r and exactly 2^r distinct rows, so the bound 'distinct rows <= 2^{rank_Q}' of S0046 is tight for arbitrary 0/1 matrices.
derivation: Index rows by x in {0,1}^r and columns by j in [r], with M_r[x,j] = x_j. The rows x = e_i (unit vectors) are the standard basis of Q^r, so rank_Q(M_r) = r (at most r columns, and r independent rows). The row indexed by x equals x itself, so the rows are pairwise distinct and there are 2^r of them. Scope: arbitrary 0/1 matrices. Not claimed: that M_r is a cut matrix of any formula or THR o THR circuit of size poly(r). Consequence: closing G0001 (poly form) needs a property of cut matrices of bounded-size circuits beyond their rank.

proved_step:
statement: Let F: {0,1}^n -> {0,1} and let S be a set of variables. Let M_S be the cut matrix with rows indexed by assignments to S, columns by assignments to the complement, and entries F. Let K(S) be the number of distinct rows of M_S and R(S) the rank over Q of M_S. Then K(S) <= 2^R(S). Consequently W(F) <= 2^R(F), where W(F) is the min over variable orders of the max over prefixes of K, and R(F) is the min over orders of the max over prefixes of R.
proof: Let r = R(S) and let V be the row space of M_S over Q, so dim V = r. Choose r linearly independent columns J of M_S. Since these columns span the column space, the submatrix M_S[:,J] has rank r, so its row space has dimension r. That row space is the image of V under the projection p_J to Q^J, so p_J is injective on V. Each distinct row of M_S is a distinct 0/1 vector lying in V, so distinct rows have distinct restrictions to J, and those restrictions lie in {0,1}^J, a set of size 2^r. Hence K(S) <= 2^r. For the consequence, take an order pi minimising the max over prefixes of R. Then the max over prefixes of K is at most 2^(max R), so W(F) <= 2^R(F). Tightness: for rows x in {0,1}^r and columns j in [r], with M[x,j] = x_j, the rank is r and K = 2^r, so the bound is attained. Scope: arbitrary Boolean functions, any n. This is the multiplicative repair of H_A and is exponential, so it does not yet give a polynomial width bound.

statement: Let F = AND of factors f_1..f_m on Boolean variables, each factor on at most 3 variables. For a variable set S let dS be the set of variables in S that occur in a factor which also contains a variable outside S. Let K(S) be the number of distinct residual functions of F on the complement, indexed by assignments to S. Then K(S) <= 2^|dS| + 1.
proof: Split factors into I (inside S), J (crossing), O (inside complement). For prefix assignment a, the residual is g(a) AND h(b) AND over f in J of f(a restricted to S cap f, b), where g(a) = AND over I of f(a) and h(b) = AND over O of f(b) does not depend on a. Each crossing factor depends on a only through a restricted to dS. So the residual is determined by the pair (g(a), a restricted to dS). If g(a)=0 the residual is the zero function (one residual). If g(a)=1 it is determined by a restricted to dS, at most 2^|dS| residuals. Hence K(S) <= 2^|dS| + 1. Consequence: min over orders of max over prefixes of K is at most 2^vs(F) + 1, where vs is the vertex separation number of the primal graph. Scope: conjunctive formulas with bounded factor size, any n. Not new: standard pathwidth-to-OBDD fact. Does not give a polynomial width for random 1-in-3 formulas, where vs is linear in n.
